advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] In resolve_jira_detection, re-apply the JIRA_URL/USER/PROJECT env overlay after the ConfigError branch so env coordinates still surface when the config load fails.
evidence: config.py:487-492: `url = user = project = ""` then `try: jira = load_config().jira; url, user, project = ... except ConfigError: pass` — no env fallback after the except
Old _cli/_jira_onboard._detect (removed): `url = os.environ.get("JIRA_URL") or url` applied unconditionally after the try/except, so env survived a ConfigError
Docstring claim contradicted: config.py:482-484 'a ConfigError degrades to the empty/env-only coordinates (fail-soft ...)' — it degrades to EMPTY, not env-only
Ticket 9515 spec: jira reads must preserve 'existing fail-soft ConfigError->env-only'
advisory.finding: resolve_jira_detection drops env-provided JIRA_URL/USER/PROJECT when the config load raises ConfigError. The old _detect() applied `os.environ.get(JIRA_URL) or url` AFTER the try/except, so a malformed config still surfaced env coordinates; the new resolver leaves url/user/project as empty strings on ConfigError and never re-reads the env. This is the exact 'wizard stays usable to FIX a bad url' path the docstring claims to preserve.
advisory.suggested_fix: After the try/except, add env-only fallback: `url = os.environ.get('JIRA_URL') or url` (and USER/PROJECT), matching the removed _detect() and the docstring's stated fail-soft behavior.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm empty-string JIRA_URL/USER/PROJECT precedence is intended vs the prior `or`-based behavior; document or reconcile the delta.
evidence: _config_sources.py:345-346: `if name in os.environ: out.setdefault(sect, {})[key] = os.environ[name]` — empty-string env is layered as an override
Old _detect(): `url = os.environ.get("JIRA_URL") or url` — an empty env value fails the `or` and the config value is kept
advisory.finding: Empty-string env precedence changed for JIRA_URL/USER/PROJECT: routing detection through load_config().jira uses env_overrides(), which includes the value whenever the var is merely PRESENT in os.environ (even empty), so JIRA_URL='' now overrides a non-empty config-file value; the old `os.environ.get(X) or url` ignored an empty env var and kept the config value.
